source: User wants ECS scalability without rebuilding the opening at Milestone 6.
decision: Move actual ECS runtime selection/foundation to Milestone 3 before inventory/salvage/research/crafting; Milestone 6 extends it.

foundationTask.name: M03.0 — Establish and prove the ECS foundation

criteria: - [ ] Compare Miniplex (first candidate) with a data-oriented alternative such as bitECS using current official APIs, TypeScript ergonomics, indexed queries, lifetime/mutation behavior, deterministic ordering, memory and plain capture/restore boundaries. Record the selected exact dependency version and measured rationale before committing feature code to its storage model; do not select by an empty-world demo alone.

- [ ] Prove representative headless/browser workloads: many inventory/buffer owners and active/idle/blocked processors, deposits/ground piles, add/remove churn, and capture/rebuild/continued steps. Use synthetic processors rather than implementing future factory gameplay. Record repeatable scale timings/allocations and view-publication overhead against the existing 20 Hz budget, with headroom; ECS adoption alone is not proof of speed or threading.

- [ ] Give Simulation one private ECS runtime and one authoritative set of component data/world resources. Use stable game-owned entity IDs and ownership links; keep queries, indexes and library handles private. Do not mirror ECS component state into a second mutable WorldState or put meshes/services/signals/DOM in components.

- [ ] Model the opening with meaningful entities/components: player bag/equipped tool and movement data, deposits, ground resource piles, handcraft/MiniFab work with real input/output/reservation state, owner links and local charge. Keep immutable content and world-level clock/ID allocation/research/history ledgers as explicit resources where appropriate. Inventory units/each technology do not need one entity each.

- [ ] Run ECS systems inside the existing authoritative fixed step, advanced by GameSession's sole 20 Hz clock. Preserve manual/current-handcraft, requested MiniFab, then Field Research spending priority and explicit structural-mutation boundaries; query iteration order is not a gameplay-priority policy. Do not register authoritative systems as Editor script tick hooks or introduce another ticker.

- [ ] Reuse the tested PlayerMotor algorithms against authoritative ECS-held movement data; keep camera/player Toolkit scripts as input/presentation bindings. Preserve existing movement, collision, picking, pause, catch-up, teardown and development-fixture behavior through focused regression checks.

- [ ] Keep recipe eligibility, slot transactions, material-value accounting and work progression as plain reusable domain rules, called by ECS systems. Handcraft, MiniFab and later factory executors share these rules with explicit policy differences; do not build duplicate inventory/crafting engines or force every executor into identical behavior.

- [ ] Publish detached projections with stable IDs through the existing GameClient/WorldView boundary. Rebuild query/index state from plain component data without importing ECS types into Angular/Babylon/contracts. Measure/select changed projections rather than making full-world cloning on every entity/system the scaling strategy.

- [ ] Define a plain component/resource capture-and-rebuild contract and verify continuation on a fresh runtime, including ID references, work/reservations/held output, research/history and charge without duplicate credits. This is groundwork for Milestone 4; no IndexedDB slots, import UI or gameplay save delivery is added here.
